name: com.tnyforge/kitchen-timer
title: Kitchen Timer
description: Plan a meal and run kitchen timers that ring on your phone. No sign-in needed to plan.

tools.name: plan_meal
tools.description: No sign-in needed. Make a meal plan: each dish starts at the right moment so everything is ready at the same time. Returns a link (open it on the phone in the kitchen, where the alarms ring), a QR code for that link, and the schedule. YOU do the cooking knowledge: break a recipe into dishes, each with its total cooking minutes, and put the timed moments inside a dish as steps ("simmer 20, rest 5" is a dish of 25 minutes with a step "Rest" at 20). Use `readyInMinutes` for "we eat in 90 minutes", `readyAt` for "at 7" (send the plain local clock time, "19:00" or "7pm"; a time zone is never needed, because the plan page fixes the exact moment in the zone of the phone that opens it, and the reply says so), or `startNow` to start cooking now (a single timer is a one-dish plan with `startNow`). If the person gave no time at all, ask when they want to eat. Keep times realistic and use only what the person gave you; at most 12 dishes, no dish over 12 hours, and a ready time up to two weeks ahead (later is refused). A clock time with no date means the next time the clock reads that on the phone that opens the plan; when the person named another day, send a local date-time such as "2026-11-24T19:00" and say the date you used. A time that has already passed (it is 8 pm and they said 7 pm, or the date is yesterday) is never an error: you get a plan for the next such time, normally tomorrow, and the reply says the day, so tell the person; if they want to eat sooner, call again with `startNow`. If the ready time is up to 15 minutes too soon for the longest dish, you still get a plan: it starts now and the reply gives the new ready time, so tell the person. If it is more than that, the reply is not an error and no plan is made: it gives the earliest ready time, so call again with `startNow` (or a later time) and tell the person the new time. For a plan more than a day away, tell the person to open the Kitchen Timer app on their phone once before the day. Dish names are plain text, no links. The reply link works for anyone who has it and the plan is deleted about a day after the meal. Tell the person the alarms ring on the phone page, not in this chat. When you wrote a recipe, send it as `recipe` (ingredients and ordered steps, with `dish` on the step that starts each timed dish): the page then shows the recipe, and Start cooking opens it on the phone with each timer inside its step and saves it under Meals. It is public like the plan, so nothing personal in it. The reply also holds a secret CONTROL KEY (starts with ktpk_): remember it for the rest of the chat, do not show it or put it in any link, and pass it with the plan's code to the control tools to keep managing this plan. Kitchen Timer can also be connected for the whole kitchen: ⋯ → Link an agent in the app shows the connector address and a 6-digit code.

dishes.description: What is being cooked. A single timer is one dish.

name.description: Plain text, 80 characters at most. For example "Roast chicken".

minutes.description: Total cooking time in minutes, from putting it in until it is done.

steps.description: Optional moments inside the cooking time, such as turning or resting.

atMinutes.description: Minutes after this dish goes in; before its total time.

startsAfter.description: Optional: this dish starts a while after ANOTHER dish instead of finishing with the meal, for example the potatoes 30 minutes after the chicken goes in. Starting that other dish early or late then moves this one with it. The other dish may not itself wait on this one.

dish.description: The other dish: its name as in this plan, or its number (1 is the first dish).

when.description: Count from when the other dish goes in, or from when it is done.

minutes.description: Minutes after that moment. 0 or left out: right then.

recipe.description: Optional: the recipe, so the person gets a full meal to cook from (ingredients, then the steps in order, each timed step showing its timer) and not only timers. It is saved under Meals on their phone when they tap Start cooking. Leave it out for a plain timer plan. Plain text only, no links. It is public like the rest of the plan (anyone with the link can read it, deleted about a day after the meal), so put nothing personal in it. Limits: 30 ingredients, 20 steps, step text 400 characters; over a limit the call is refused, nothing is cut.

title.description: The name the meal is saved under in Meals, 80 characters at most. Left out: the dish names.

summary.description: One or two sentences about the dish, 300 characters at most.

ingredients.description: Ingredient lines with quantities, for example "1.8 kg chicken". At most 30, 100 characters each.

steps.description: The method in order, at most 20 steps. A step that puts a dish on to cook sets `dish` and so starts that dish's timer; a hands-on step (chop, season, rest, serve) has no `dish`.

title.description: A short heading, 80 characters at most. Left out: the start of the text.

text.description: What to do, 400 characters at most.

dish.description: Only on the step that starts a dish's timer: that dish's position in `dishes`, counting from 0 (the first dish is 0). Each dish at most once. The time is the dish's own `minutes`; never repeat it here.

readyInMinutes.description: Everything ready this many minutes from now. Give exactly one of readyInMinutes, readyAt, startNow.

readyAt.description: Everything ready at this time: a plain local clock time such as "19:00" or "7pm" (no time zone needed: the phone that opens the plan fixes the moment), a local date-time such as "2026-10-17T19:00" for another day, ISO 8601 with a UTC offset (2026-10-17T19:00:00+01:00), or epoch milliseconds.

startNow.description: True: start every dish now (the longest dish sets when it is ready).

timeZone.description: Optional IANA time zone such as Europe/London. Leave it out when you do not know it: a plain local clock time needs no zone, the phone page fixes the moment. Only used to word the schedule text; the card and the phone show times in the viewer's own clock.

tools.name: meal_status
tools.description: No sign-in needed. Say what is next in a meal plan made with plan_meal, and how long until it. Give the plan's code (the last part of its link). Only reads; never changes a plan. Give the control key too, if you have it, to also see the timers on the phone.

code.description: The plan's code, or its whole link.

key.description: Optional: the plan's secret control key. With it the answer also says whether the person has started the timers on the phone and what each one is doing.

tools.name: pause_meal
tools.description: No sign-in needed. Pause every dish of this plan that is running on the phone (the cook can resume on the phone or you can call resume_meal). Needs the plan's code and control key. Only works after the person has tapped Start on the phone; before that it says so.

code.description: The plan's code, or its whole link.

key.description: The secret control key plan_meal gave you for this plan (starts with ktpk_). Never show it or put it in a link.

tools.name: resume_meal
tools.description: No sign-in needed. Resume the paused dishes of this plan on the phone. Needs the plan's code and control key.

code.description: The plan's code, or its whole link.

key.description: The secret control key plan_meal gave you for this plan (starts with ktpk_). Never show it or put it in a link.

tools.name: adjust_dish
tools.description: No sign-in needed. Add time to a dish (a positive number of minutes) or take time off (negative). Before the person taps Start this changes the plan, and the ready time stays; afterwards it changes that dish's timer on the phone. Needs the plan's code and control key.

code.description: The plan's code, or its whole link.

key.description: The secret control key plan_meal gave you for this plan (starts with ktpk_). Never show it or put it in a link.

dish.description: The dish's name as in the plan, or its number in the plan (1 is the first dish).

minutes.description: Minutes to add (positive) or take off (negative), such as 2 or -1.5. Not zero.

tools.name: skip_step
tools.description: No sign-in needed. Skip the rest of the current wait for one dish: a dish still waiting to go in starts now, and a dish that is cooking finishes now. Only works after the person has tapped Start on the phone. Needs the plan's code and control key.

code.description: The plan's code, or its whole link.

key.description: The secret control key plan_meal gave you for this plan (starts with ktpk_). Never show it or put it in a link.

dish.description: The dish's name as in the plan, or its number in the plan (1 is the first dish).

tools.name: add_dish
tools.description: No sign-in needed. Add one more dish to this plan. The ready time stays, so the new dish goes in at the ready time minus its cooking time and must still fit. Before the person taps Start it joins the plan on the sheet; afterwards it goes onto the phone too. Same rules as plan_meal: a plain-text name, at most 12 dishes. Needs the plan's code and control key.

code.description: The plan's code, or its whole link.

key.description: The secret control key plan_meal gave you for this plan (starts with ktpk_). Never show it or put it in a link.

steps.description: Optional moments inside the cooking time.

tools.name: link_dish
tools.description: No sign-in needed. Make a dish start a while after another dish goes in or is done ("the potatoes 30 minutes after the chicken goes in"), or clear that link by leaving `after` out. Starting the other dish early or late then moves this one with it. A dish cannot wait on a dish that waits on it, and a dish that already started cannot be linked. Needs the plan's code and control key.

code.description: The plan's code, or its whole link.

key.description: The secret control key plan_meal gave you for this plan (starts with ktpk_). Never show it or put it in a link.

dish.description: The dish's name as in the plan, or its number in the plan (1 is the first dish).

after.description: The dish to follow: its name as in the plan, or its number. Leave out to clear this dish's link.

when.description: Count from when that dish goes in, or from when it is done.

minutes.description: Minutes after that moment. 0 or left out: right then.

tools.name: cancel_meal
tools.description: No sign-in needed. Cancel this plan: its link stops working, and if the person already started it, its timers are removed from the phone. Only that plan's timers; nothing else on the phone. Needs the plan's code and control key. Ask the person first.

code.description: The plan's code, or its whole link.

key.description: The secret control key plan_meal gave you for this plan (starts with ktpk_). Never show it or put it in a link.

tools.name: kitchen_status
tools.description: Needs the phone link: the person signs in with the 6-digit code from the Kitchen Timer app (⋯ → Link an agent). What's cooking right now: every timer with time left, the next buzz, and whether the phone's backup alarm is armed. Call this first — it returns the server clock, the kitchen's timezone, and the ids and labels every other tool accepts.

include.description: Extra sections. 'settings' the kitchen defaults; 'changelog' recent app releases (the What's new list); 'laps' the full flip log per timer instead of just a count; 'devices' every paired phone and its push health. Default: none — live timers only, which is the cheap common call.

tools.name: list_cookbook
tools.description: Needs the phone link: the person signs in with the 6-digit code from the Kitchen Timer app (⋯ → Link an agent). Saved presets (reusable single timers) and meals (named groups of dishes) in one call, with each meal's dishes resolved to real names and durations. Read this before start_timers, start_meal, edit_cookbook or delete_saved.

search.description: Optional case-insensitive filter on preset label, meal name, or dish label. Omit to return everything.

limit.description: Max rows per section. Keep it small; large results get truncated by the client.

tools.name: list_history
tools.description: Needs the phone link: the person signs in with the 6-digit code from the Kitchen Timer app (⋯ → Link an agent). Past timer runs — completed and stopped early — newest first, grouped by day, with planned vs actual time. For what is running now use kitchen_status.

limit.description: How many runs to return. Paginate with 'before' rather than raising this.

before.description: Paging cursor: only runs that ended before this time. Pass the nextBefore value from a previous call. Accepts an ISO timestamp, a clock time read in the kitchen's timezone ('9am', '18:30' — today), or a relative form ('90m ago', '-2h').

after.description: Only runs that ended at or after this time. Use for 'what did I cook today?' — pass '00:00'. Accepts an ISO timestamp, a clock time read in the kitchen's timezone (resolved to today), or a relative form ('90m ago', '-2h').

label.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on the run's label, e.g. 'rice'.

outcome.description: 'completed' ran to the end; 'stopped' was abandoned early. Omit for both.

summaryOnly.description: true returns per-day counts and totals with no individual rows.

tools.name: start_timers
tools.description: No sign-in needed. For timers made up on the spot (a label and a duration, started now) it makes a link that rings in the browser on the phone in the kitchen, one link per timer, and if the person signs in later those timers move to their phone. With the phone linked (the 6-digit code from the Kitchen Timer app, ⋯ → Link an agent) it starts the timers on the phone itself, and the phone is alerted even when it is asleep. Saved presets, stopwatches, repeating buzzes, steps and idle (startNow false) timers need the phone link. For a whole saved meal use start_meal.

label.description: What is cooking, e.g. 'Rice'. Shown on the phone's lock-screen notification. Defaults to 'Timer'.

colour.description: The timer's card colour. Omit and it gets the next colour no timer on the board uses.

stopwatch.description: Make a stopwatch instead of a countdown: it counts UP from 0, has no deadline and never rings. Give no duration, every, steps or manualFlips with it. Drive it with control_timers: start, pause (resume with start), flip = lap, reset, delete.

duration.description: How long, WITH A UNIT: '8m', '90s', '1h30m', '1.5 hours'. A number without a unit is rejected. Required unless 'steps' is given.

every.description: Buzz repeatedly at this interval WITHOUT shortening the timer, e.g. '5m' (minimum 5s). Use for 'stir every 5 minutes'. Do not combine with steps or manualFlips.

steps.description: Buzz at each stage boundary, e.g. ['2m','4m','4m'] for sear-2 then flip-every-4. Total run time is the SUM of the steps, so do not also send 'duration'. There is no buzz at the final boundary — the finish alert covers it. Do not combine with every or manualFlips.

manualFlips.description: Enable a hand-logged flip list with no automatic buzzing; log flips later with control_timers action 'flip'. Do not combine with every or steps.

sound.description: 'off' means vibrate and notification only. Only these two values do anything.

vibrate.description: Vibrate the phone when the timer finishes.

rings.description: How many times the finish alarm repeats before giving up. Default 10.

presets.description: Names or ids of saved presets to start (see list_cookbook). Each one's use count is bumped, as tapping it in the app would.

startNow.description: true runs them immediately. false creates them idle so the cook taps Start — this is what the app's Load button does.

notify.description: Send one notification to the cook's phone that these timers were started. Default true — a timer the cook never learns about is a trap.

tools.name: start_meal
tools.description: Needs the phone link: the person signs in with the 6-digit code from the Kitchen Timer app (⋯ → Link an agent). Put a saved meal's dishes on the timer board. Give a ready time and each dish is back-timed so they all finish together — dishes that should already be cooking start immediately, the rest get a start reminder that buzzes the phone when it is their turn.

meal.description: Meal id or name from list_cookbook. Case-insensitive; an ambiguous name is an error listing the candidates.

readyAt.description: Finish together: when the whole meal should be ready. Accepts a clock time ('6:30 PM', '18:30'), a relative time ('in 90m'), or an ISO timestamp. Clock times are read in the kitchen's timezone, which kitchen_status returns. A clock time already in the past is an error, never rolled to tomorrow: for another day send an ISO date-time (up to two weeks ahead; later is refused). If the person gave only a clock time that has passed today, take the next such time or ask which day, and state the date you chose in your answer. For a plan more than a day away, tell the person to open the Kitchen Timer app on their phone once before the day.

startNow.description: Only used when readyAt is omitted. true starts every dish now; false loads them idle so the cook starts them (the app's Load behaviour).

only.description: Optional subset of dish names to load, e.g. ['Roast potatoes']. Omit to load every dish.

notify.description: Notify the cook's phone that the meal is on.

tools.name: control_timers
tools.description: Needs the phone link: the person signs in with the 6-digit code from the Kitchen Timer app (⋯ → Link an agent). Change timers that already exist: start, pause, reset, restart, log a flip, silence, or delete. Select them by name or id, or by state. To add or remove time use adjust_timer instead. To make a dish that has not started wait for another (the potatoes 30 minutes after the chicken goes in) use action `link` with `startsAfter`; `unlink` clears it. Starting the other dish early or late then moves the linked dish with it. kitchen_status shows each link as startsAfterTimerId / startsAfterWhen / startsAfterMinutes.

action.description: start — run an idle timer or resume a paused one. pause — freeze a running timer, keeping the time left, and cancel its backup alarm. reset — back to idle at full duration, discarding the flip log; NOTE this abandons a live run WITHOUT recording it in history, matching the app. restart — run a finished timer again from the top. flip — log a manual flip on a running timer without changing the deadline. silence — stop the alarm ringing without changing the timer. delete — remove the timer entirely; unlike reset, an abandoned live run IS recorded in history as stopped early.

timers.description: Timer ids or labels from kitchen_status. Case-insensitive; an ambiguous label is an error listing the candidates. Give this or 'scope', not both.

scope.description: Act on every timer in this state instead of naming them. scope 'idle' with action 'start' is the app's 'Start all' button. Give this or 'timers', not both.

startsAfter.description: Only with action `link`: the dish to follow. The linked timer must be idle or waiting (not started), and the other timer may not itself wait on it.

timer.description: The other timer's id or label from kitchen_status.

when.description: Count from when the other timer starts, or from when it finishes.

minutes.description: Minutes after that moment. 0 or left out: right then.

notify.description: Buzz the phone about this change. Default false — the cook usually asked for it out loud.

tools.name: adjust_timer
tools.description: Needs the phone link: the person signs in with the 6-digit code from the Kitchen Timer app (⋯ → Link an agent). Add or remove time on one timer, e.g. '+2 minutes'. Moves the deadline and the total length together. On a finished timer, adding time re-runs it for exactly that long.

timer.description: Timer id or label from kitchen_status. Case-insensitive; an ambiguous label is an error listing the candidates.

by.description: Signed duration WITH A SIGN AND A UNIT: '+2m', '-30s', '+1h'. Positive adds time, negative removes it. Removing more time than is left finishes the timer.

tools.name: edit_cookbook
tools.description: Needs the phone link: the person signs in with the 6-digit code from the Kitchen Timer app (⋯ → Link an agent). Create or update saved presets and meals in one call. Saving never starts anything. Omit the id/name of an existing item to create a new one; include it to update, and fields you leave out keep their current values.

preset.description: Id or name of an existing preset to UPDATE. Omit to create a new one.

label.description: Preset name, e.g. 'Basmati rice'. Required when creating.

colour.description: The preset's card colour; timers started from it wear it.

duration.description: How long, with a unit: '12m', '1h30m'. Required when creating unless 'steps' is given.

every.description: Buzz repeatedly at this interval without shortening the timer (minimum 5s). Do not combine with steps or manualFlips.

steps.description: Stage boundaries, e.g. ['2m','4m','4m']. Total duration is their sum, so do not also send 'duration'. Do not combine with every or manualFlips.

manualFlips.description: Hand-logged flip list, no automatic buzzing. Do not combine with every or steps.

reminders.description: Pass 'none' to CLEAR all reminders from an existing preset. Omitting every/steps/manualFlips on an update leaves reminders unchanged.

alert.description: Finish-alert overrides. Preserved on update unless you send a new one.

rings.description: How many times the finish alarm repeats.

meal.description: Id or name of an existing meal to UPDATE. Omit to create a new one.

name.description: Meal name, e.g. 'Sunday roast'. Required when creating.

emoji.description: Icon shown on the meal card. Defaults to a plate.

presets.description: Names or ids of saved presets to include as dishes. On update this REPLACES the current list; omit it to leave it unchanged; pass [] to remove all preset dishes. Unknown names are an error, never silently dropped.

notes.description: The meal's note (a tip for the whole meal). '' clears it. Omit to leave it unchanged.

presetDishes.description: Words on this meal's PRESET dishes (they belong to the meal, not to the preset): what to do at that dish and a note. Each item names a preset already in the meal. '' clears a field; an omitted field is unchanged.

preset.description: A preset name or id that is one of this meal's presets.

instruction.description: One short line: what to do at this dish.

note.description: A tip, may have line breaks.

order.description: The meal's dishes in cooking order, naming each by its preset name or one-off dish name. Set startsAfterAbove on a dish that must begin when the dish above it FINISHES (egg, then ice bath); the other dishes finish together. Omit to leave the order unchanged; changing `dishes` without `order` clears the order marks.

dish.description: A preset name or one-off dish name already in this meal.

startsAfterAbove.description: Start this dish when the dish above it finishes. Ignored on the first dish.

dishes.description: One-off dishes belonging to this meal only, NOT added to the preset library. On update this REPLACES the current list; omit to leave unchanged; pass [] to remove all.

instruction.description: One short line: what to do at this dish. '' clears it; omitted keeps the words this dish has now.

note.description: A tip for this dish, may have line breaks. '' clears it; omitted keeps the current one.

every.description: Optional buzz interval for this dish.

steps.description: Optional stage boundaries for this dish.

manualFlips.description: Optional hand-logged flip list for this dish.

tools.name: delete_saved
tools.description: Needs the phone link: the person signs in with the 6-digit code from the Kitchen Timer app (⋯ → Link an agent). Permanently delete a saved preset or meal. Deleting a preset also removes it from every meal that used it. Timers already on the board are unaffected. Run history is cleared with clear_history.

kind.description: Which library item to delete. Presets are single reusable timers; meals are named groups of dishes; a recipe is a meal with steps (only while recipes are switched on for the phone).

item.description: Id or name of the preset or meal. Case-insensitive; an ambiguous name is an error listing the candidates with their ids.

tools.name: clear_history
tools.description: Needs the phone link: the person signs in with the 6-digit code from the Kitchen Timer app (⋯ → Link an agent). Permanently delete past run history — all of it, everything older than a date, or all but the newest N runs. There is no undo. Requires confirm: true.

confirm.description: Must be true. Guards against an accidental wipe: there is no undo and no client-side backup.

before.description: Delete only runs that ended before this time. Accepts an ISO timestamp, a clock time read in the kitchen's timezone (resolved to today), or a relative form ('7d ago', '-24h'). Omit to consider all runs.

keepLatest.description: Keep only the N most recent runs and delete the rest.

entries.description: Delete exactly these history entry ids (from list_history).

tools.name: update_settings
tools.description: Needs the phone link: the person signs in with the 6-digit code from the Kitchen Timer app (⋯ → Link an agent). Change kitchen defaults: the alert used by new timers (sound, volume, vibration, rings, saying the timer's name), the theme, the screen wake lock, and the Android background keep-alive. Takes effect on the phone the next time the app is opened.

defaultAlert.description: Stamped onto newly created timers and presets. Existing timers keep their own alert.

sound.description: The alarm sound. 'off' means vibrate and notification only.

rings.description: How many times the finish alarm repeats before giving up.

volume.description: In-app alarm volume in percent, for when the app is open (never below 10).

speak.description: Say the timer's name between rings, while the app is open.

theme.description: The app's look: auto follows the phone.

wakeLock.description: Keep the phone screen awake while a timer runs and the app is in front.

keepAlive.description: Play a silent audio loop so Android does not freeze the app in the background. Costs a media notification and some battery.

tools.name: send_report
tools.description: Needs the phone link: the person signs in with the 6-digit code from the Kitchen Timer app (⋯ → Link an agent). Send feedback or a bug report to the app's developer on the cook's behalf. Goes into the same triage queue as the in-app form, tagged as agent-submitted.

kind.description: 'feedback' for an opinion or request; 'bug' for something broken.

message.description: What the cook wants to say, in their own words where possible.

rating.description: Feedback only. How they feel about the app overall.

severity.description: Bug only. 'blocking' means they cannot cook with it.

steps.description: Bug only. How to reproduce it.

contact.description: Optional email so the developer can reply. Only include it if the cook offers one — never invent one.

tools.name: save_recipe
tools.description: Needs the phone link: the person signs in with the 6-digit code from the Kitchen Timer app (⋯ → Link an agent). Save a recipe — a meal with ordered steps the cook follows on the phone, each step able to start its own timer — or edit one. Give the steps as pasted text (`text`, one step per numbered line or paragraph), as a link to a recipe page (`url`), or as `steps`. A time written in a step ("roast for 45 minutes"; a range like "2-3 hours" takes the upper end) becomes that step's timer, the same as pasting it into the app. Saving never starts anything. To edit, name the recipe in `recipe`: fields you leave out keep their value; `text`, `url` or `steps` REPLACE all the steps (a run in progress keeps its place).

recipe.description: Id or name of an existing recipe to EDIT (see read_recipes). Omit to create a new one.

name.description: Recipe name. Required when creating from text or steps; from a link it defaults to the page's title.

emoji.description: Icon on the recipe card. Defaults to a plate.

summary.description: One short line describing the dish.

text.description: The recipe steps pasted as text: numbered or bulleted lines, else paragraphs. Times in a step become that step's timer.

url.description: A web address of a recipe page (http or https). The server reads the page's recipe data; links to private or internal addresses are refused. Ten a minute.

steps.description: Steps given directly. Use this when you have already split the recipe yourself.

title.description: Short step name, e.g. 'Boil the potatoes'.

text.description: The full instruction, if the title is not enough.

duration.description: Give the step a timer of this length, with a unit: '15m', '1h30m'. Omit for a step with no timer.

tools.name: read_recipes
tools.description: Needs the phone link: the person signs in with the 6-digit code from the Kitchen Timer app (⋯ → Link an agent). List the saved recipes (name, number of steps and timers, whether the cook is part-way through one), or give `recipe` to read one in full: every step with its text and timer, and the step the cook is on right now. Plain meals are not listed here — list_cookbook has those.

recipe.description: Id or name of one recipe to read in full. Omit to list them all.

search.description: When listing: case-insensitive filter on the recipe name.

tools.name: cook_recipe
tools.description: Needs the phone link: the person signs in with the 6-digit code from the Kitchen Timer app (⋯ → Link an agent). Move through a recipe the way the cook does on the phone, on the same shared state: whichever of you moves the step, the other sees it after the phone's next sync. `start` begins a run at step 1 (or continues the one in progress; with `step`, at that step), `next`/`back` move one step (`next` on the last step finishes), `goto` jumps to `step`, `timer` starts the timer of the current step (or of `step`) on the board with an absolute finish time, and `finish` ends the run (timers already running keep running).

recipe.description: Id or name of the recipe (read_recipes).

action.description: What to do; see the tool description.

step.description: A step number, counting from 1. Required for `goto`; optional for `start` and `timer`.

notify.description: Only for `timer`: notify the cook's phone that the timer is on.

tools.name: arrange_timers
tools.description: Needs the phone link: the person signs in with the 6-digit code from the Kitchen Timer app (⋯ → Link an agent). Change where a timer sits on the Timers tab (`up` or `down`, one place, the way ⋯ → Move up / Move down does) or add a ready, not-started copy of it directly below (`duplicate`: "Pasta" becomes "Pasta 2", same time, steps, flip settings and alert; no run, meal or link). A dish of a meal moves only inside its own meal, and not once the meal is under way.

timer.description: Timer id or label from kitchen_status.

action.description: up / down — one place; duplicate — a copy directly below.

tools.name: share_saved
tools.description: Needs the phone link: the person signs in with the 6-digit code from the Kitchen Timer app (⋯ → Link an agent). Make the link the app's Share button makes, for a saved preset or meal: the cook can send it to a friend, whose app offers to add it. The link only carries the definition (names, times, steps, reminders, colours) in the part after the #, which no server ever sees; it carries no id, no use count, no alert settings, no notes and no way into this kitchen. Nothing is stored or sent.
